title: The Key to High Performance: What the Data Says - Dr. Nicole Forsgren
summary: Forsgren summarizes four years of State of DevOps findings: no speed-stability tradeoff, architecture over platform, culture and leadership predict performance.

assertions.quote: we find that software delivery performance is through putting stability and both are possible without trade-offs
high performers year over a year are twice as likely to achieve or exceed their commercial goals

verdicts.note: DORA finds this association in self-reported data; organizational performance is reported by the same respondents, so common-method bias is possible.

DORA's SEM finds SDO performance predicts organisational performance on commercial and non-commercial goals, and elite performers are twice as likely to meet or exceed their organisational performance goals; both sides are self-reported in a cross-sectional survey.

assertions.quote: if we create maturity models they go out of date too fast

verdicts.note: An argument about how to frame a transformation, not a measured outcome.

assertions.quote: they have a much smaller blast radius and it's much much easier to identify what those changes are
we need technology and process and culture to really get this strong synergy

verdicts.note: DORA's models and Bessen's HBR work support IT-plus-management, but the specific synergy is modeled, not experimentally shown.

The report's model has culture of psychological safety, a clear change process and cloud implementation (only 29% of self-described cloud users met the NIST characteristics that actually predict performance) all driving delivery performance, and tells organisations to start with automation plus clear change approval and a healthy culture.

The review's strongest evidence, from studies of mature agile teams, is that success requires attention to human and social factors (balanced autonomy, trust, interpersonal skills); it concerns agile adoption rather than technology investment.

assertions.quote: the thing that is most important is having a loosely coupled architecture both at the team level and at the technology level

verdicts.note: DORA 2017 found architecture the strongest predictor of continuous delivery while mainframe and greenfield status were not significant; still survey-based.

DORA revalidated that a loosely coupled architecture, defined as teams independently testing, deploying and changing their systems without depending on other teams, positively predicts continuous delivery; the 2019 report does not rank it against platform or technology choice.

assertions.quote: these are the ones that we have seen are predictive of your ability to develop and deliver software with both speed and stability
number one or number two biggest constraint for most teams is a lightweight change approval process

verdicts.note: DORA 2019 found external approvals correlated with worse performance and no better stability; correlational.

Respondents whose organisations require CAB or senior-manager approval were 2.6 times more likely to be low performers, formal approval showed no association with lower change failure rates, and a clear, lightweight change process made teams 1.8 times more likely to be elite.

assertions.quote: the generative group was most highly correlated with high performance

verdicts.note: Westrum culture measures predict performance in DORA's structural models, with survey-based data.

A culture of psychological safety (measured with Google's Project Aristotle items) predicts software delivery performance, organisational performance and productivity, extending earlier years' finding that a Westrum generative culture of information flow, trust and risk-sharing predicts SDO performance.

assertions.quote: leadership is necessary but not sufficient

verdicts.note: DORA found the bottom third of leaders half as likely to be high performers while top leaders were no better than median; one survey year.

assertions.quote: less deployment pain less burnout higher employee Net Promoter Score

verdicts.note: Self-reported associations in DORA data; direction of causation is not established.

The highest performers are half as likely to report feeling burned out, and good technical practices and clear change management reduce burnout in the model; deployment pain and willingness to recommend the workplace were studied in earlier years, not here.
